- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or misses upward momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% to capture rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a 5–10% downward correction.
- If model shows strong mean reversion bias (e.g., forecasting back to 65–67 after 70+), check sentiment for reversal signals — if sentiment shifts to positive, allow slight upward drift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price action; adjust final 5–7 days upward if sentiment is bullish or volatility is rising.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, -0.33, 1.00), model may misread trend direction; use sentiment-weighted average for smoothing.
